clue.text: A bar is gripped by male artist's dance

indicators.note: the A and the bar are held between the letters of the male, as if clutched in his hands

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a male
to bar something is to ban it
RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword's standard artist

explanation.surface: A ban on a bar by some male painter is somehow connected to a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is gripped by' puts A BAN inside HE, giving H-ABAN-E, then RA follows. RA stands for a member of the Royal Academy, Britain's academy of artists.
explanation.definitionFit: The habanera is a slow Cuban dance and song form in duple time, made famous by Bizet's Carmen.

clue.text: Country that made a scholar out of young Williams

indicators.note: the degree letters are placed outside the boy's name, so he is made into a scholar

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate scholar
Eric Williams is the schoolboy hero of Farrar's Victorian novel Eric, or Little by Little

explanation.surface: Some nation turned a boy named Williams into a learned man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made a scholar out of' means giving the boy a degree to wrap round him. Eric, or Little by Little is an 1858 English school story whose hero is Eric Williams.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is commonly called by this shorter name.

clue.text: Drink beer very quietly inside lift

indicators.note: inside places the musical marking within the word for beer

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet
to jack up a car is to lift it

explanation.surface: Someone sips beer on the sly in an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' signals the musical marking for pianissimo going into the beer; 'lift' is the verb, as with a car jack.
explanation.definitionFit: Applejack is an American brandy distilled from cider.

clue.text: English cleric receiving the French team

indicators.note: the English clergyman takes in the French word, holding it between his letters

parts.note: Ven., Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An English clergyman takes in a French side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' has the English clergyman take in the French article. Ven. (Venerable) is the formal title of an archdeacon in the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side has this many players, so the number stands for the team.

clue.text: A natural event involving a discharge, obviously

parts.note: matter is pus, the discharge from a wound
of course means naturally, obviously

explanation.surface: Something natural happens when a wound weeps, as anyone can see.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition uses the first 'A'; the second 'a' starts the wordplay. 'discharge' looks electrical but is medical matter, pus.
explanation.definitionFit: Something expected and routine, which happens in the normal run of things.

clue.text: Merlin was wonderful!

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at the magician's performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Merlin is the sorcerer of Arthurian legend, and the word for a sorcerer is also old British slang exclaiming that something is splendid.

clue.text: Undisciplined violation of rules reported in game

parts.note: wild means unruly

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word for a breach is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a foul is an infringement in sport

explanation.surface: Unruly behaviour and a foul play in a sports match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like sport but means hunted birds; 'reported' turns FOUL into its sound-alike FOWL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducks and geese shot for sport are game birds.

clue.text: Object appearing in two forms in 26

explanation.surface: Something that shows up twice in another clue's answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 across is RATHER, which holds both A and THE, the two English articles.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is a thing or item, and in grammar it is a word like the or an.

clue.text: Paints for a month at old charges?

parts.note: Dec is short for December
rates are fees or prices

explanation.surface: Doing up a house for a month costs what used to be charged?
explanation.walkthrough: Rates were the old British property tax, which gives the question mark its point.
explanation.definitionFit: To decorate a room is to paint or paper it.

clue.text: Place for a lawyer or an archbishop

explanation.surface: Where might one find a barrister, or a senior churchman?
explanation.walkthrough: The Inner and Middle Temple are two of the Inns of Court where London barristers work; William Temple (and his father Frederick) were Archbishops of Canterbury.
explanation.definitionFit: One London legal precinct shares its name with two twentieth-century heads of the Church of England.

clue.text: Main light almost installed in upper room?

indicators.note: the shortened word is fitted inside the room like a fixture being installed

parts.note: an attic is the room at the top of a house

indicators.note: almost tells us to stop one letter short of the full word

parts.note: to light on something is to land on it, as a bird alights

explanation.surface: A lamp has nearly been fitted in the loft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like a lamp but is the verb, to alight on something; 'almost' drops its last letter and 'installed in' fits the rest into the loft.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is an old poetic word for the open sea, and this ocean is the one between Europe and America.

clue.text: Sentence leads to strike — it prevents someone going down

parts.note: a life sentence is a term of imprisonment for life
to belt someone is to hit them

explanation.surface: A prison term provokes violence, and something saves a person from sinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A buoyant ring thrown to someone in the water keeps them from drowning.

clue.text: Swordsman erecting a wooden barrier

explanation.surface: A man with a sword is putting up a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencer duels with a foil or sabre, and the same word can describe a worker who puts up fences.

clue.text: Shock about a hard Asian prince

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for shock is read backwards

parts.note: a jar is a jolt or shock
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A tough Asian ruler is given a jolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the jolt round; 'Shock' looks like a noun of hair or surprise but is a jolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A rajah is an Indian king or ruling prince.

clue.text: Comeback from woman feeding animals out east

indicators.note: the woman goes into the animals as food goes into a mouth
out says one letter is dropped from the animals

parts.note: reindeer are deer of the Arctic
E is the compass abbreviation for east
Jo is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A girl gives food to beasts in the east and gets a sharp reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes one of the two Es from the deer, and 'feeding' puts the woman's name into them after their first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort or sharp reply to someone's remark.

clue.text: Scots Wren's curious station on board?

indicators.note: curious here means odd or strange, signalling that the letters are put into an unusual order

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A Scottish member of the women's naval service has an odd post aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curious' rearranges the nine letters of SCOTS WREN. A Wren was a member of Britain's Women's Royal Naval Service, which keeps the naval scene in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A lookout platform high on a ship's mast is where a sailor is stationed to watch.

clue.text: It carries a handle on a door

definitions.text: It carries a handle on a door

parts.words: It carries a handle on a door
parts.note: handle is slang for a name, so this is a sign fixed to a door, not a doorknob

explanation.surface: A door fitting that bears a knob.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaque giving the occupant's name, screwed to a front or office door.

clue.text: No traces, possibly, of one farther up the tree

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: No sign at all of someone higher in the family tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges NO TRACES.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear comes earlier in a family line, drawn higher on a genealogical chart.

clue.text: Dive from a cutter

explanation.surface: Plunging from a small boat called a cutter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive where the body folds and straightens shares its name with a large folding pocket knife.

clue.text: Manage to wield the stick

explanation.surface: To run things by waving the baton.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct is to manage a business, and also to direct an orchestra with a baton.

clue.text: Animal crossing motorway? That's out of order

indicators.note: the animal straddles the road, its letters on either side of it

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A donkey wandering across the motorway is clearly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' has the donkey straddle the road. The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amiss is wrong or not as it should be.

clue.text: Voluptuous nurse has customary opening withdrawn

parts.note: SEN was a State Enrolled Nurse in Britain

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for customary is taken away

parts.note: usual means customary

explanation.surface: A sultry nurse always used to begin by pulling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening withdrawn' drops the first U of USUAL, leaving SUAL. SEN was a grade of nurse in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensual means given to physical pleasure, full-bodied and sexy.

clue.text: Not like this clue for a trial

explanation.surface: Unlike a down clue, and also a burden.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue is a down clue, so it is not of the other kind; read as two words, the answer is a cross, a trial to bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Grid entries run either down or sideways; a cross is a burden or ordeal one carries.

clue.text: Natural place for drink at end of game

parts.note: an inn serves drinks

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word game

explanation.surface: Going to the pub after the match is only natural.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' gives E, the last letter of 'game'.
explanation.definitionFit: An innate quality is inborn, present by nature.

clue.text: Tenant gives officer award a set of books

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding
a cup is a trophy
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A lodger presents a commander with a trophy and a library.
explanation.walkthrough: NT is the New Testament, a set of books within the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant is the person living in a house or flat, its resident.

clue.text: "My —! O my ducats! O my —!" (M. of Ven.)

definitions.text: "My —! O my ducats! O my —!" (M. of Ven.)

parts.words: "My —! O my ducats! O my —!" (M. of Ven.)
parts.note: fill both gaps in Shylock's lament from The Merchant of Venice, when his child elopes with his money

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare with the same word missing twice.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Merchant of Venice, Shylock cries this when Jessica runs off with Lorenzo and his money; Solanio mocks him by repeating it.
explanation.definitionFit: Jessica is Shylock's child, the girl he mourns alongside his stolen coins.

clue.text: Obscure work in Paris that includes 7

indicators.note: the French word and the work together enclose the article from the cross-referenced clue

parts.note: op. is short for opus, a work
que is French for that
the answer to 7 down is a part of speech, and A is one of its forms

explanation.surface: A dark piece of writing in Paris involves some object.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 down supplies the indefinite article; 'includes' sets it between the work and the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque means not letting light through, hence murky or hard to understand.

clue.text: It's in the river at Hereford, to some extent

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Something is found in the river Wye at Hereford, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'It's' as the definition and 'to some extent' as the indicator; but 'to some extent' means the answer, and 'It's in' signals the letters inside 'river at Hereford'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather means somewhat or to a certain degree, as in rather cold.

clue.text: See about plant in this wind

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the see wraps round the flower

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire
an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: Look at the vegetation growing in this breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like an instruction to look; it is a bishop's see, Ely, an English cathedral city. 'about' puts ASTER inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind blowing from the east is named for the direction it comes from.
